chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Thawrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

If the water in the well-reservoir is a kurr, nothing renders it impure. I said: And how much is the kurr? He said: Three spans and a half in its length, by three spans and a half in its depth, by three spans and a half in its width.

This report may bear two possibilities: one of them is that what is meant by al-rakī is the constructed reservoir that does not have a supply from a spring, as opposed to wells that do have a supply from it; for that is what consideration of kurr applies to, as we have explained. The second is that this may have been issued in the context of taqiyyah, because among the jurists are those who equate wells and ponds in their smallness and abundance, so it is possible that the report was issued in agreement with them. What clarifies that is that al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, the narrator of this hadith, is a Zaydī, Batrī, whose hadith is abandoned in what he is alone in narrating.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in outward expression
key_terms.الرَّكِيِّ: the well-reservoir or excavated water source mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْحَدِيثِ: the report or hadith being examined
key_terms.الْفُقَهَاءِ: the jurists whose view is referenced in the discussion
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the substance whose ritual purity ruling is being discussed
key_terms.زَيْدِيٌّ: a Zaydī affiliation attributed here to the narrator
key_terms.كُرًّا: the measure of water that reaches the threshold at which impurity does not affect it
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it impure in the legal sense

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Istibṣār say about kurr water in a well, and how is it interpreted?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal threshold of kurr water and states that water in a well-reservoir is not rendered impure if it reaches that amount. The passage then presents two ways of understanding the report, including that it may refer specifically to a reservoir without spring supply or that it may have been stated under taqiyyah, while also noting a weakness related to its narrator.
